title: PTE Academic Listening — Practice Test 22
topic: Mixed academic topics (one per item, as in the real test)
instructions: Each item has its own recording. Audio plays automatically when you reach an item.

questions.prompt: Item 1: Coral Bleaching and Ocean Temperatures
questions.audioScript: Coral bleaching occurs when seawater temperatures rise above normal levels, causing corals to expel their symbiotic algae. This symbiosis provides corals with nutrients through photosynthesis. Recent data shows that even a one-degree Celsius increase can trigger bleaching events. The Great Barrier Reef experienced severe bleaching in 2016 and 2020. Scientists attribute this to climate change and rising ocean temperatures. Recovery is possible if temperatures stabilize within weeks.
questions.modelAnswer: Coral bleaching happens when water temperatures rise, causing corals to lose their symbiotic algae. Even minimal temperature increases trigger bleaching events. The Great Barrier Reef suffered severe bleaching recently due to climate change, though recovery is possible if temperatures stabilize quickly.

questions.audioScript: Roman aqueducts were masterpieces of civil engineering, carrying water across hundreds of kilometers to supply cities. The longest aqueduct, Aqua Claudia, stretched 68 kilometers, though only 16 were elevated on arches. Romans used gravity to move water downhill, maintaining a slight slope of about 0.3 percent. Lead pipes transported water into homes, a practice later recognized as toxic. These structures demonstrate remarkable architectural knowledge and mathematical precision that lasted for centuries.
questions.modelAnswer: Roman aqueducts transported water across vast distances using gravity and innovative engineering. The Aqua Claudia extended 68 kilometers with arches supporting only the elevated sections. Romans maintained precise slopes and used lead pipes, later found hazardous. These structures showcase exceptional mathematical and architectural skill that persisted for centuries.

questions.audioScript: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. The process occurs in two main stages: light-dependent reactions in the thylakoid and light-independent reactions in the stroma. During light reactions, chlorophyll absorbs photons, splitting water and releasing oxygen. Light-independent reactions, or the Calvin cycle, fix carbon dioxide into glucose. Only about 1-2 percent of incident light energy converts to plant biomass. Factors like light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, and temperature affect photosynthetic rate.
questions.question: According to the speaker, which TWO statements accurately describe photosynthesis?
options: Photosynthesis occurs entirely in the stroma
Chlorophyll absorbs photons during light reactions
Carbon dioxide is fixed in the Calvin cycle
Photosynthesis achieves 50 percent energy conversion
Oxygen is produced from carbon dioxide splitting
correctAnswers: Chlorophyll absorbs photons during light reactions
Carbon dioxide is fixed in the Calvin cycle
questions.explanation: The speaker correctly describes light reactions involving chlorophyll and photons, and mentions the Calvin cycle for carbon fixation.
questions.prompt: Item 3: Photosynthesis Efficiency and Carbon Fixation

questions.audioScript: The Great Pyramids of Giza remain monumental achievements of ancient engineering. The Great Pyramid of Khufu required approximately 20 years to construct using 2.3 million stone blocks. Workers quarried limestone blocks weighing up to 2.5 tons. Construction methods likely involved ramps, levers, and organized labor systems. Precise geometric alignment demonstrates advanced mathematical knowledge. These structures served as monumental tombs housing pharaohs and treasures. Archaeological evidence suggests tens of thousands of workers participated in construction.
questions.question: According to the speaker, which TWO claims about the pyramids are supported?
options: Construction used only 100,000 stone blocks
The Great Pyramid required 20 years to build
Individual blocks weighed up to 2.5 tons
Construction methods were entirely mysterious
Precise alignment shows mathematical knowledge
correctAnswers: The Great Pyramid required 20 years to build
questions.explanation: The speaker explicitly states the 20-year construction period and describes precise geometric alignment demonstrating mathematical knowledge.
questions.prompt: Item 4: Ancient Egyptian Pyramids and Construction
Item 5: Particle Physics and Quantum Mechanics
questions.audioScript: Particle physics studies fundamental constituents of matter at the smallest scales. The Standard model describes quarks and leptons as basic building blocks. Subatomic particles are held together by fundamental forces carried by force-carrying particles. The discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 confirmed theories predicting how particles acquire mass through interaction with an energy field.
questions.transcript: Particle physics studies fundamental constituents of matter at the smallest scales. The __1__ model describes quarks and leptons as basic building blocks. Subatomic particles are held together by fundamental forces carried by __2__ particles. The discovery of the Higgs __3__ in 2012 confirmed theories predicting how particles acquire mass through interaction with an energy field.
questions.explanation: The missing words, in order, are: Standard, force-carrying, boson. You hear each one as the recording plays the full passage.

questions.audioScript: Tropical rainforests contain approximately half of Earth's terrestrial species despite covering only seven percent of land. The dense canopy of plants creates multiple layers where different species have evolved specialized roles. Trees compete for limited light by growing tall, while lianas and epiphytes use other plants for access. The rich soil is paradoxically fragile because nutrients are rapidly absorbed by living plants; decomposed material is recycled quickly by decomposers and fungi.
questions.transcript: Tropical rainforests contain approximately half of Earth's terrestrial species despite covering only seven percent of land. The dense __1__ of plants creates multiple layers where different species have evolved specialized roles. Trees compete for limited __2__ by growing tall, while lianas and epiphytes use other plants for access. The rich soil is paradoxically fragile because nutrients are rapidly absorbed by living plants; decomposed material is recycled quickly by __3__ and fungi.
questions.explanation: The missing words, in order, are: canopy, light, decomposers. You hear each one as the recording plays the full passage.

questions.audioScript: The Industrial Revolution transformed production from craft-based to mechanized manufacturing. The steam engine, invented by James Watt, powered machines and transportation, providing mechanical energy previously unavailable on such scales. Textile mills combined multiple production steps in one location, dramatically increasing output per worker. Factory systems relied on division of labor performing repetitive tasks, establishing the modern industrial workforce structure.
questions.transcript: The Industrial Revolution transformed production from craft-based to mechanized manufacturing. The steam engine, invented by James Watt, powered machines and transportation, providing __1__ energy previously unavailable on such scales. Textile __2__ combined multiple production steps in one location, dramatically increasing output per worker. Factory systems relied on __3__ labor performing repetitive tasks, establishing the modern industrial workforce structure.
questions.explanation: The missing words, in order, are: mechanical, mills, division of. You hear each one as the recording plays the full passage.

questions.audioScript: Biotechnology harnesses microorganisms and enzymes for industrial manufacturing. Fermentation produces ethanol, dairy products, and antibiotics using bacterial or fungal cultures. Enzyme-based processes break down biomass into usable chemicals and fuels. Genetic engineering optimizes organisms for specific production tasks. Bioreactors provide controlled environments maximizing productivity. These processes offer environmentally friendly alternatives to petroleum-based manufacturing.
options: Industrial biotechnology uses microorganisms and enzymes in fermentation and genetic engineering to produce chemicals and fuels sustainably.
Biotechnology relies exclusively on natural microorganisms without modification, making industrial applications impossible to optimize.
Chemical synthesis from petroleum remains more environmentally friendly than any biotechnological manufacturing process.
questions.correctAnswer: Industrial biotechnology uses microorganisms and enzymes in fermentation and genetic engineering to produce chemicals and fuels sustainably.
questions.explanation: The speaker describes fermentation, enzyme processes, and genetic engineering for sustainable production alternatives.

questions.audioScript: Metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks undergo chemical and physical changes due to heat, pressure, or chemical alteration deep within Earth's crust. High pressure and temperature cause mineral rearrangement without melting the rock. Parent rocks include sedimentary and igneous types. Examples include marble from limestone and schist from shale. Metamorphic rocks contain distinctive mineral alignments reflecting directional pressure. These rocks mark ancient collision zones and deep crustal processes.
options: All metamorphic rocks contain fossils unchanged from their parent rocks despite extreme geological conditions.
Metamorphic rocks form from existing rocks altered by heat and pressure deep in Earth, producing distinctive mineral alignments.
Metamorphic rocks form when sedimentary rocks melt completely into magma, then recrystallize near the surface.
questions.correctAnswer: Metamorphic rocks form from existing rocks altered by heat and pressure deep in Earth, producing distinctive mineral alignments.
questions.explanation: The speaker explains metamorphic rocks result from heat and pressure altering parent rocks without melting, creating distinctive structures.

questions.audioScript: Photochemical reactions in the stratosphere produce and destroy ozone through light-driven processes. Ultraviolet radiation breaks oxygen molecules into atoms. Two oxygen atoms recombine with an oxygen molecule to form ozone. Ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation protecting the surface. Chlorofluorocarbons release chlorine atoms when exposed to ultraviolet light. These chlorine atoms catalytically destroy ozone molecules. The ozone hole over Antarctica results from seasonal chlorine release.
questions.question: What is the primary mechanism by which chlorofluorocarbons harm the ozone layer?
options: They combine with oxygen to form additional ozone, creating excess ultraviolet penetration
They directly absorb ultraviolet radiation preventing photochemical reactions
They release chlorine atoms that catalytically destroy ozone molecules
They increase the temperature of the stratosphere beyond ozone stability
questions.correctAnswer: They release chlorine atoms that catalytically destroy ozone molecules
questions.explanation: The speaker explains that chlorine atoms released from CFCs catalytically destroy ozone molecules.

questions.audioScript: Roman law established principles of justice that influenced Western legal systems. The Twelve Tables, created around 450 BC, codified Roman legal principles. Roman law distinguished between public law governing the state and private law regulating individuals. Legal concepts including contracts, property rights, and due process originated in Rome. The Roman Senate served as the legislative body making laws. Consuls acted as chief executives with military and administrative powers. This system of separated powers influenced modern democratic structures.
questions.question: Which aspect of Roman law most directly influenced modern Western legal systems?
options: Unlimited executive power without legislative oversight
Religious courts rather than secular legal institutions
The absence of written legal codes allowing interpretation flexibility
Principles including contracts, property rights, and due process formalized in codes
questions.correctAnswer: Principles including contracts, property rights, and due process formalized in codes
questions.explanation: The speaker describes Roman law's establishment of justice principles like contracts and due process that influenced Western systems.
questions.prompt: Item 11: Ancient Roman Law and Government

questions.topic: Climate Change and Rising Sea Levels
questions.prompt: Item 12: Climate Change and Rising Sea Levels
questions.audioScript: Global temperatures continue rising due to greenhouse gas emissions from human activities. Warming oceans expand thermally, increasing sea level. Melting glaciers and ice sheets contribute additional water to the oceans. Coastal communities face increased flooding threats from rising sea levels. Some island nations risk complete submersion within decades. We must reduce emissions and develop adaptation strategies for inevitable changes.
options: adaptation
mitigation
prevention
reversal
questions.explanation: The speaker concludes that we need adaptation strategies for inevitable sea level changes.

questions.prompt: Item 13: Personal Learning and Study Strategies
questions.audioScript: Effective learning requires active engagement with material rather than passive reading. Spaced repetition strengthens memory through repeated review across days and weeks. Elaboration connects new information to existing knowledge creating meaningful understanding. Interleaving mixes different topics during study improving discrimination between concepts. Practice problems strengthen skill development. Teaching others forces deep processing of knowledge. The most successful students combine multiple evidence-based study techniques for optimal learning …
options: understanding
outcomes
achievement
retention
questions.explanation: The speaker concludes that combined techniques produce optimal learning outcomes.

questions.audioScript: Medieval castles served strategic defensive purposes in warfare. Stone walls could withstand siege weapons far better than wooden palisades. Multiple defensive layers including moats, walls, and towers provided overlapping fields of fire. Narrow windows called arrow slits allowed defenders to shoot while remaining protected. The keep provided a final defensive position if outer walls were breached. High walls prevented direct assault and made scaling extremely difficult. Castles dominated their territories militarily and politically for centuries.
questions.displayTranscript: Medieval castles served strategic offensive purposes in warfare. Stone walls could withstand siege weapons far better than wooden palisades. Multiple defensive layers including moats, walls, and towers provided overlapping fields of view. Narrow windows called gun slits allowed defenders to shoot while remaining protected. The dungeon provided a final defensive position if outer walls were breached. Low walls prevented direct assault and made scaling extremely difficult. Castles dominated their territories militarily and politically for centuries.
questions.explanation: Castles were defensive, used for fire control, had arrow slits and keeps, and had high walls for protection.

questions.audioScript: Evolution occurs through natural selection acting on genetic variation within populations. Organisms producing more offspring than the environment supports must compete for resources. Traits that improve survival and reproduction become more common across generations. Over millions of years, accumulated changes produce new species. Fossil records document transition forms showing evolutionary relationships. Genetic evidence confirms common ancestry across all living organisms. Evolution explains the diversity of life and shapes our understanding of biology.
questions.displayTranscript: Evolution occurs through artificial selection acting on genetic variation within populations. Organisms producing fewer offspring than the environment supports must compete for resources. Traits that decrease survival and reproduction become more common across generations. Over thousands of years, accumulated changes produce new species. Fossil records document transition forms showing revolutionary relationships. Chemical evidence confirms common ancestry across all living organisms. Evolution explains the simplicity of life and shapes our understanding of biology.
questions.explanation: Natural selection increases beneficial traits over millions of years through evolutionary relationships.
